prs.cluster_pick_reason: Implements a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that correctly handles Accept header semantics: splits on ',' and ';' params, honors q=0 exclusion, and matches type/subtype (including wildcards) case-insensitively. #2046's fix uses a naive acceptHeader?.includes('application/json') substring check, which can false-positive on unrelated media types containing that substring (e.g. 'application/json-patch+json') and does not respect q=0 weighting or wildcard matching. #1996 is the more spec-compliant implementation of the same fix, so it should be kept and #2046 closed as duplicate.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add src/index.ts re-exporting types.js and inMemory.js, but #2030 additionally does `export * from './client/index.js'` and `export * from './server/index.js'`. Both client/index.ts and server/index.ts re-export shared symbols from the shared protocol module (Protocol/ProtocolOptions/RequestOptions etc.), so barreling both through the root index causes duplicate-export collisions (TS2308) and would fail the build. #2523's comment explicitly documents this and keeps Client/Server on their existing ./client and ./server subpath exports instead of re-exporting them at root. #2523 also ships a changeset describing the fix and its scope; #2030 has no changeset. #2030's root test asserts `Client`/`Server` are importable from the root barrel, which is exactly the assertion that would break once the TS2308 collision is fixed, so its test coverage encodes the wrong target API.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add src/index.ts re-exporting types.js and inMemory.js, but #2030 additionally does `export * from './client/index.js'` and `export * from './server/index.js'`. Both client/index.ts and server/index.ts re-export shared symbols from the shared protocol module (Protocol/ProtocolOptions/RequestOptions etc.), so barreling both through the root index causes duplicate-export collisions (TS2308) and would fail the build. #2523's comment explicitly documents this and keeps Client/Server on their existing ./client and ./server subpath exports instead of re-exporting them at root. #2523 also ships a changeset describing the fix and its scope; #2030 has no changeset. #2030's root test asserts `Client`/`Server` are importable from the root barrel, which is exactly the assertion that would break once the TS2308 collision is fixed, so its test coverage encodes the wrong target API.
